recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Convert to degrees and reduce
steps.margin_note: Degrees are easier here because 18° and 54° are the standard angles whose exact sines are known. The last two come out negative.

recall.must_convey: That the four angles are converted to 18°, 54°, −54° and −18° in cosine form.
accept: convert to degrees, eighteen and fifty four, and the last two are negative
cos seven pi by ten is minus cos fifty four and cos nine pi by ten is minus cos eighteen
change to degrees and reduce the obtuse ones
degrees ga marchi, chivari rendu minus vasthai
the four angles become plus and minus eighteen and fifty four

steps.why: Radians hide the fact that these are the pentagon angles. Converting is what makes the exact values recognisable.
common_mistakes: Staying in radians and missing the standard values.

steps.label: Pair into differences of squares
steps.margin_note: First mark. Same pairing as answer 67 — each plus bracket with its own minus partner.

recall.must_convey: That the brackets pair into (1 − cos²) forms, giving sin²18° sin²54°.
accept: pair each bracket with its negative to get one minus cos squared which is sin squared
the product becomes sin squared eighteen times sin squared fifty four
pair them into differences of squares
pairs cheste sin square eighteen into sin square fifty four vasthundi
each pair gives a sine squared

steps.why: Identical move to answer 67 — the two questions are the same shape with different angles.

steps.label: Substitute the exact values
steps.margin_note: sin18° = (√5 − 1)/4 and sin54° = (√5 + 1)/4. These are standard results and are quoted, not derived.

recall.must_convey: That the standard exact values sin18° = (√5−1)/4 and sin54° = (√5+1)/4 are substituted.
accept: substitute sin eighteen equals root five minus one over four and sin fifty four equals root five plus one over four
use the standard exact values for the two sines
quote the known values of sin eighteen and sin fifty four
sin eighteen and sin fifty four exact values substitute cheyyali
the two sines have known surd values

steps.why: These two values are conjugates, which is why their product is rational — that is what makes the whole expression collapse to a simple fraction.
common_mistakes: Trying to derive the values instead of quoting them.

steps.label: Multiply out and simplify
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Group the two conjugates together first: (√5 − 1)(√5 + 1) is 5 − 1 = 4, and the surds vanish.

recall.must_convey: That the conjugates multiply to 5 − 1 = 4, giving (4/16)² = 1/16.
accept: root five minus one times root five plus one is four so it becomes four over sixteen all squared which is one sixteenth
the conjugates give five minus one equals four and the answer is one over sixteen
multiply the conjugates first then square
conjugates multiply cheste four vasthundi, answer one by sixteen
the answer is one sixteenth

steps.why: Multiplying the conjugates BEFORE squaring is what keeps the arithmetic clean — squaring each surd first would work but is far messier.
